fixtures.name: Satisfiable-instance witness finder promoted to decider
fixtures.invalid_inference: The algorithm finds a witness whenever one exists, therefore it decides SAT.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Termination and rejection correctness on unsatisfiable instances are absent.
fixtures.witness: A semidecision procedure may run forever on NO instances.
fixtures.remediation: Prove total halting and both YES and NO correctness under the WP00 language convention.

fixtures.name: No-case certificate or halting proof omitted
fixtures.invalid_inference: The solver never returns a false satisfying assignment, so it decides SAT.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Soundness of positive outputs does not prove completeness, rejection correctness, or total halting.
fixtures.witness: A solver that always answers UNKNOWN is sound but decides nothing.
fixtures.remediation: Supply a total correctness proof for all encoded inputs.

fixtures.name: Benchmark or average performance promoted to worst-case P
fixtures.invalid_inference: The method solves almost all sampled formulas quickly, therefore SAT is in P.
fixtures.missing_obligation: P requires one worst-case polynomial bound over every input of each length.
fixtures.witness: A distribution can assign negligible probability to an adversarial infinite family.
fixtures.remediation: State the distributional result or prove a worst-case theorem and any required reduction.

fixtures.name: Finite verification promoted to asymptotic separation
fixtures.invalid_inference: All instances through size B were checked, so P differs from NP.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Infinitely many unverified lengths remain and a finite table can be hard-coded.
fixtures.witness: Every finite language lies in P regardless of behaviour beyond the checked bound.
fixtures.remediation: Report a bounded certificate only or prove an asymptotic lower bound.

fixtures.name: Shannon counting promoted to an explicit NP lower bound
fixtures.invalid_inference: Almost all Boolean functions need exponential circuits, therefore SAT does.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The counting argument does not identify or analyze the explicit SAT language.
fixtures.witness: A sparse, explicitly defined class can lie entirely inside the exceptional set left by an almost-all theorem.
fixtures.remediation: Connect an explicit NP language to the lower-bound property with a theorem-grade argument.

fixtures.name: Monotone lower bound promoted to unrestricted circuits
fixtures.invalid_inference: An exponential monotone circuit lower bound proves an unrestricted lower bound.
fixtures.missing_obligation: General circuits may use negation and cancellation forbidden in the monotone model.
fixtures.witness: The monotone and unrestricted circuit complexities of a function can differ exponentially.
fixtures.remediation: Retain the monotone conclusion or prove a lifting theorem to unrestricted circuits.

fixtures.name: AC0 lower bound promoted to general circuits
fixtures.invalid_inference: Parity requires exponential AC0 size, therefore it is outside P/poly or P.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Unrestricted circuits may use depth growing with input size and other gates.
fixtures.witness: Parity has small unrestricted Boolean circuits despite its AC0 lower bound.
fixtures.remediation: Preserve the constant-depth model or prove an explicit escalation theorem.

fixtures.name: AC0[p] lower bound promoted to unrestricted circuits
fixtures.invalid_inference: A lower bound against constant-depth MOD_p circuits settles NP versus P/poly.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The theorem excludes only a fixed restricted gate/depth model.
fixtures.witness: General circuits can have arbitrary depth and gate composition.
fixtures.remediation: State the AC0[p] result exactly and identify any valid transfer theorem separately.

fixtures.name: NEXP not in ACC promoted to NP not in P
fixtures.invalid_inference: A nonuniform lower bound for NEXP against ACC circuits proves P is not NP.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Both the language class and the circuit model differ from the terminal target.
fixtures.witness: A separation high in the exponential hierarchy can coexist logically with unresolved P versus NP.
fixtures.remediation: Retain the NEXP/ACC theorem or supply every downward and model-transfer bridge.

fixtures.name: Depth-two threshold lower bound promoted to NP separation
fixtures.invalid_inference: A super-quadratic THR-of-THR lower bound for a language in E^NP proves an NP language lacks polynomial circuits.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The explicit language is in a larger class and the lower bound concerns a restricted depth-two threshold model.
fixtures.witness: The theorem does not exclude general polynomial-size circuits for SAT.
fixtures.remediation: Record the exact E^NP and THR-of-THR scope; supply a separate downward transfer before any P-versus-NP claim.

fixtures.name: Near-maximum restricted lower bound promoted to NP separation
fixtures.invalid_inference: A near-maximum circuit lower bound for E^{prMA}/1 resolves P versus NP.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The complexity class, advice, and circuit restriction do not match NP versus unrestricted polynomial-time computation.
fixtures.witness: A very strong lower bound can remain nonterminal when proved for a higher class or narrower model.
fixtures.remediation: Preserve all class, advice, success-probability, and circuit-model qualifiers.

fixtures.name: Hardness magnification conclusion asserted without its premise
fixtures.invalid_inference: Because a magnification theorem exists, a major circuit lower bound has been proved.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The required modest lower-bound premise for the explicit meta-complexity problem is not established.
fixtures.witness: An implication A implies B proves neither A nor B by itself.
fixtures.remediation: Prove the exact premise in the specified model or keep the statement conditional.
